arguments.criteria: Exactly two concise findings. Finding 1: a visual observation of the blue object's shape/location, citing the image. Finding 2: measured image width and height in pixels, citing the supplied telemetry ID, not the image. Each observation and recommendation under 10 words. No scene-size guesses or reasoning text. Structured JSON only.

arguments.description: Verify attached image hash and byte count

arguments.command:
python - <<'PY'
from PIL import Image
from collections import Counter
path = '.proscenium/artefacts/sha256/fab5fe51c19b8a3a1ef87f388679d9520a6b6d5badabcae9d517244359782bcc/content'
im = Image.open(path).convert('RGB')
points = [(x,y) for y in range(im.height) for x in range(im.width) if (lambda r,g,b: b > 110 and b > r*1.4 and b > g*1.15)(*im.getpixel((x,y)))]
print('Image dimensions:', im.size)
print('Blue pixels:', len(points))
if points:
    xs, ys = zip(*points)
    print('Blue bounds:', min(xs), min(ys), max(xs), max(ys))
    rows = Counter(y for x,y in points)
    print('Blue row widths:', [(y,rows[y]) for y in range(min(ys),max(ys)+1, max(1,(max(ys)-min(ys))//8))])
    print('Common blue colors:', Counter(im.getpixel(p) for p in points).most_common(3))
PY
arguments.description: Read blue object pixel geometry without modifying files

arguments.command:
python - <<'PY'
from PIL import Image
im = Image.open('.proscenium/artefacts/sha256/fab5fe51c19b8a3a1ef87f388679d9520a6b6d5badabcae9d517244359782bcc/content').convert('RGB')
for y in range(0,360,10):
    row = ''
    for x in range(0,640,10):
        r,g,b = im.getpixel((x,y))
        row += '#' if b > 110 and b > r*1.4 and b > g*1.15 else ' '
    print(row.rstrip())
PY
